review_comment: I'd make them `GUAGE` and `COUNTER` and `HISTOGRAM` just to follow along with normal java stuff. You'd have to convert to upper case on parse but I think that's fine.

I started writing this change, but it turned out that code became a lot more complicated just to convert input to upper case and also convert enum values to lower case when logging error messages. Otherwise, user receives error messages like the following:

`"Unknown value [histogram] for field [time_series_metric] - accepted values are [GAUGE, COUNTER]"` 

So, sticking to enum names same as the expected input values would result in a a lot simpler code.

We have followed the same approach [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/5baabff6670a8ed49297488ca8cac8ec12a2078d/x-pack/plugin/mapper-aggregate-metric/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/aggregatemetric/mapper/AggregateDoubleMetricFieldMapper.java#L93-L101)
Oh well. I don't like it there either! But I think it's cool - they can stay lowercase.

It can also become relatively simple  if I replace the generic implementation (`restrictedEnumParam()`) from `FieldMapper` class and only add the custom implementation for the `MetricType` enum in the `TimeSeriesParams`.

Is a more specific to `MetricType` implementation with capitalized names  a better approach here?

Sorry I don't understand - do you mean that you can either share the enum infrastructure or capitalize the names of the constants? If that's the case I think I prefer sharing the enum infrastructure. That way if we come up with a clever way to capitalize the names we can get it in a follow up and hit everything using the infrastructure.

@romseygeek can you please have a look at this and let me know what you think?

I thought this could be re-usable
So so so many parameters. Nothing you can do about it now, but we should think about something cleaner eventually.
I agree it's ugly. I can create a new constructor with default values (`false` and `null`) for the time series parameters. WDYT?

I'm not at all sure! Maybe a builder or some test utility methods or something.

I don't think it's a problem for this PR though. It seems like a great candidate for a follow up change.
It's probably worth adding a test to `ParameterizedMapperTests`.
